source_text:
(8) Στίχ. κβ΄. Εἶπε δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἵλεως ὑμῖν, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
Ἔοικεν ὠφεληθῆναι ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰς θεοσέβειαν παρὰ τῷ Ἰωσήφ.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Genesis 43:23, where Joseph's steward reassures the brothers, and he observes that this man seems to have benefited in piety from Joseph.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 22. He said to them: Mercy to you, do not be afraid. This man seems to have been benefited in piety with Joseph.

choices.why: The adjective ἵλεως is used as a greeting or reassurance meaning 'mercy be to you' or 'be gracious'; rendering it as a noun phrase preserves the force of the steward's reassurance without turning it into a verb.
The aorist passive infinitive indicates a completed benefit received by the steward; the perfective sense is preserved with 'to have been benefited'.
The preposition εἰς with the accusative indicates the sphere or goal of the benefit; 'in piety' captures the sense that the steward grew in godly reverence.
The preposition παρά with the dative indicates proximity or association; 'with Joseph' conveys that the benefit came through his presence or influence.

bible_refs.note: Εἶπε δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἵλεως ὑμῖν, μὴ φοβεῖσθε

pass_b_english: He said to them, “Mercy to you; do not be afraid” (Genesis 43:23). This man seems to have been benefited in piety by Joseph.

problems.quote: This man seems to have been benefited in piety with Joseph.
problems.source_quote: Ἔοικεν ὠφεληθῆναι ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰς θεοσέβειαν παρὰ τῷ Ἰωσήφ.
problems.why: Greek ‘παρὰ τῷ Ἰωσήφ’ means ‘by Joseph’, not ‘with Joseph’, changing who causes the benefit.
problems.fix: This man seems to have been benefited in piety by Joseph.
problems.ruling: παρὰ τῷ Ἰωσήφ means 'by Joseph' as agent, not 'with Joseph'; translation reverses who benefits whom.

edits.old: This man seems to have been benefited in piety with Joseph.
edits.new: This man seems to have been benefited in piety by Joseph.

fixed: Changed 'with Joseph' to 'by Joseph' because the Greek παρὰ τῷ Ἰωσήφ indicates Joseph as the agent of the benefit, not merely a companion.
